title: A bill to amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act with respect to the scope of new chemical exclusivity.
official_summary:
This bill provides statutory authority for the existing Food and Drug Administration (FDA) practice of defining active ingredient more narrowly as active moiety in certain situations, such as when determining whether a new drug is entitled to a market exclusivity period or providing priority review of drugs for treating rare pediatric diseases.

Generally, the FDA defines active moiety as the core molecule or ion in a drug responsible for the relevant physiological or pharmacological action. By contrast, the FDA defines an active ingredient as a component in a drug that is intended to furnish pharmacological activity or other direct effect. The FDA's existing practice of interpreting active ingredient as active moiety in certain situations, as statutorily authorized by this bill, tends to exclude some drugs from market exclusivity.

The bill replaces references to active ingredient with active moiety in various statutes authorizing FDA activities.

summary.headline: This law sets in statute an FDA practice of using the narrower term "active moiety" instead of "active ingredient" when deciding certain drug market exclusivity and priority review questions.
summary.what_it_does: The FDA already defined drugs this way in some cases. This law gives that practice explicit legal authority. It replaces "active ingredient" with "active moiety" in several laws that govern FDA activities. Under the narrower term, some drugs may not qualify for market exclusivity.

who_it_affects.group: Drug companies that develop new drugs
who_it_affects.how: Whether a new drug qualifies for a market exclusivity period can depend on the narrower active moiety definition.
Because exclusivity periods block generic competitors for a set time, a narrower definition can affect when generic versions of some drugs may enter the market.

who_it_affects.group: Families of children with rare pediatric diseases
who_it_affects.how: The narrower term also applies to decisions about priority review for drugs treating these diseases, which can affect how quickly those drugs are reviewed.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not give a separate effective date. The law was enacted on April 23, 2021.
